title: Post-Merger Workforce Integration

source.note: Transcript on p256, approach page on p257

prompt: The client is a legacy newspaper player that has recently acquired a digital media firm. They seek your advice on the integration of both companies.

facts.asks: Each firm's offering and the goal of the acquisition
facts.reveal: The client prints a national daily with a pan-India presence. Because readership growth is stagnant at 1–2%, they wanted to move into the digital space. The acquired firm mainly covers entertainment news for a younger internet audience and has a mobile application. Its revenue is about 50% of the client's, and it is poised to grow at 10% a year, compounded, over the next 10 years.

facts.asks: Which problem to work on, once the candidate has laid out the areas of integration
facts.reveal: This seems comprehensive. Focus on people-related and systems-related issues. The client wants to know how to allocate the workforce in the combined entity.

Both firms have marketing, legal, finance and HR consolidated at their headquarters. The legacy firm lacks a digital-strategy function, which the newer firm has, but it has distributor-relations and publishing functions. The legacy firm has a geographic divisional structure, with each region a distinct profit centre and content generated at the regional level. The digital firm's content generation is split by type: entertainment, tech, business and so on.
Based on this, how would you integrate the workforce?

facts.asks: After the candidate proposes a separate digital division
facts.reveal: Why do you recommend a separate division for it? What else do you suggest with the organisational structure?

facts.asks: Size of the overlap, when the candidate raises redundancy
facts.reveal: Assume 60% of roles in overlapping functions are redundant post-integration. How would you proceed?

facts.asks: After the candidate proposes a fitment test
facts.reveal: How do you assess who will be better suited for each role? What should be done with those in redundant roles who don't clear the fitment test?
Highlight briefly a few initiatives to improve the integration of employees in the merged entity.

acceptedAssumptions: Digital at 10% a year for 10 years becomes about 2.5 times its size; print grows about 15% in total

crux.statement: Structure follows growth. Digital gets its own division (autonomy, accountability, authority) next to a Traditional division that keeps its regional structure. A unified content-strategy team spans both, headquarters functions are consolidated, and digital reuses regional content.
crux.clue: The growth gap: 10% a year for digital against 1–2% for print.

paths: New structure → redundancy elimination → integration initiatives (the source's route)
Any sequence that settles structure before cutting roles

wrongTurns.text: Folding both firms into one structure

quant.working: Derived: 1.1 to the power 10 is about 2.6 times for digital; print at 1–2% for 10 years is about 1.10 to 1.22 times. With digital starting at 50% of print's revenue: 0.5 × 2.6 = 1.3 against about 1.1 to 1.2, so digital overtakes print within the decade.
quant.answer: Digital grows about 2.6 times and overtakes print within the decade

answerKey: Redundancy: a fitment test by seniority (junior roles on technical skills, middle managers on interpersonal skills, leadership on conceptual skills)
Evidence from external feedback (peers, superiors, subordinates, panels) and internal records (ratings, trajectory, situational or technical tests)
Those who do not clear it: an alternative role at the same level, the option to step down a level, or temporary roles; layoffs last

Employee level: training and development (equal pay and incentives across divisions, cross-training, access to management, knowledge sharing) and redressal (personal channels, cross-firm engagement sessions)
Organisation level: resource symmetry (systems, technology, processes) and culture symmetry (working styles, norms)

close.condition: The candidate has proposed a structure and a way to handle redundant roles.
close.prompt: Summarise your recommendation on structure, redundancy and integration.

anchors.s7: A sensible structure and a fitment process.
anchors.s9: Uses the growth maths to justify the separate division, gives a humane redundancy sequence, and names specific integration initiatives.

verifierFlags.text: 60% of overlapping roles redundant in the transcript (p256); 50% on the approach page (p257).
"Bringing in 50% of the client's revenue" is ambiguous.
verifierFlags.decision: Read as: the digital firm's revenue is about half of the print firm's. The candidate's maths (digital overtakes print within a decade) only works on this reading.

verifierFlags.text: In the transcript the candidate, not the interviewer, lists the four integration areas.
verifierFlags.decision: The interviewer does not list them. A correction to the BRD's section 4 is already proposed there.
